results.name: weaviate
results.title: Weaviate
results.summary: Go-based AI-native vector database — stores objects with vectors, integrated vectorization via OpenAI/Cohere/HuggingFace modules, semantic + BM25 keyword + hybrid search, built-in RAG and reranking, ACORN filtered search, multi-tenancy with RBAC, object TTL, gRPC/REST/GraphQL APIs; BSD-3-Clause

results.name: mixpeek
results.title: Mixpeek
results.summary: Multimodal search/retrieval infrastructure ('multimodal data warehouse') running on object storage: typed feature-extraction pipelines turn video/files into queryable timestamped features (scenes, transcripts, faces, OCR, fingerprints), embeddings are generated/stored from 50+ models, and multi-stage retrievers compose filter/join/rerank (advertised <100ms). Integrations include S3, GCS, R2, Mux, LangChain, and MCP. Catalog source is a Mixpeek education video contrasting an 'extract once, upstream of every app' model against a plain vector database.

results.name: supabase
results.title: Supabase
results.summary: Open-source Postgres development platform (Firebase alternative) with built-in auth, storage, realtime, edge functions, REST/GraphQL APIs, and pgvector AI toolkit — massive community (36K+ commits), self-hostable, Apache-2.0

results.name: pinecone
results.title: Pinecone
results.summary: Fully managed, closed-source serverless vector database — proprietary Rust engine separates compute from storage, consumption-based pricing (~$0.33/GB-month storage plus metered read/write units), targets ~200ms query latency at 80% p95 recall; offers hosted embedding/reranking (Pinecone Inference), Pinecone Assistant, Dedicated Read Nodes, and Bring-Your-Own-Cloud for data residency; no self-hosting option.

results.name: turbopuffer
results.title: turbopuffer
results.summary: Serverless vector and full-text search database built object-storage-first (S3/GCS/Azure Blob as source of truth, ~$0.02/GB) with an NVMe SSD and RAM caching hierarchy layered on top — cold namespaces cost near-zero, hot namespaces get sub-10ms p50 cached-query latency; write-ahead log on object storage for durability (~10K+ vectors/sec writes), strong consistency by default; no free tier, $64/month minimum; proprietary, no self-hosted version; production users include Cursor (95% cost reduction after migrating from Pinecone), Anthropic, Notion, Linear.

results.name: qdrant
results.title: Qdrant
results.summary: Rust-based vector similarity search engine and database — HNSW with inline payload filtering, dense/sparse/multi-vector search, hybrid search with RRF/DBSF fusion, TurboQuant 4-bit/8-bit compression, GPU-accelerated indexing, distributed sharding and replication, gRPC and REST APIs, Edge variant for in-process use; Apache-2.0

results.name: milvus
results.title: Milvus
results.summary: Go/C++ cloud-native vector database — fully distributed K8s-native architecture, HNSW/IVF/DiskANN/CAGRA GPU indexes, dense + sparse + BM25 full-text + hybrid search, lake-native data access (v3.0) with Apache Iceberg/Parquet/Lance, multi-tenancy with hot/cold storage, Milvus Lite for embedded use; LF AI and Data Foundation; Apache-2.0

results.name: pgvector
results.title: pgvector
results.summary: PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search — HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, exact and approximate nearest neighbor, vector/halfvec/bit/sparsevec types, 6 distance functions (L2/IP/cosine/L1/Hamming/Jaccard), iterative index scans, binary quantization, multitenancy via partitioning, hybrid search with pg full-text; all Postgres guarantees (ACID, JOINs, WAL replication); PostgreSQL License

results.name: chroma
results.title: Chroma
results.summary: AI-native open-source embedding database — 4-function core API, automatic tokenization/embedding/indexing, metadata filtering, in-memory or persistent modes, SIMD-accelerated maxscore, sharding, group-by aggregation, Python/JS/Go clients; Chroma Cloud for managed serverless; Apache-2.0

results.name: lancedb
results.title: LanceDB
results.summary: Embedded serverless vector database built on Lance columnar format — runs in-process with no server, IVF/HNSW/PQ/RQ vector indexes + BM25 full-text, multimodal columns (text/image/video/audio), Git-style versioning, zero-copy reads, object storage backend (S3/GCS/AZ), DuckDB SQL integration, Python/TypeScript/Rust/REST SDKs; Apache-2.0

results.name: chromadb
results.title: ChromaDB
results.summary: Open-source AI search infrastructure with vector, full-text, regex, and hybrid search — embedding-agnostic with Python/JS SDKs, serverless cloud option, and multi-modal retrieval; strong fit for literature/sequence RAG pipelines

results.name: neo4j
results.title: Neo4j
results.summary: Native property-graph database storing data as labeled nodes and typed relationships with key-value properties, queried via Cypher (now standardized as ISO GQL); open-core licensing — Community Edition (GPLv3) covers ACID transactions, native graph storage/indexing, vector and full-text indexes, and APOC's 450+ procedures, while Enterprise Edition (commercial license) adds role-based auth, LDAP/Kerberos, Causal Clustering, tens-of-billions-scale graphs, rolling upgrades, and hot backup; also offered as AuraDB managed cloud and a newer Infinigraph Edition with unlimited horizontal sharding; Graph Data Science library ships as a separate open-core component (Community: all algorithms, 4-CPU cap, 3-model catalog limit; Enterprise: unlimited cores, cluster write support).

results.name: vespa
results.title: Vespa
results.summary: Open-source (Apache-2.0) big-data serving engine from Yahoo (open-sourced 2017, spun out as Vespa.ai in 2023) combining hybrid search (BM25 keyword + vector + tensor operations), real-time indexing, and machine-learned multi-phase ranking at billions-of-documents scale with sub-100ms latency; stateless container clusters handle query/indexing logic separately from stateful content clusters holding the data; available self-hosted or as Vespa Cloud; used in production by Spotify, Perplexity, Etsy, and others.

results.name: pageindex
results.title: PageIndex
results.summary: Vectorless reasoning-based RAG engine — replaces vector index with hierarchical tree index, uses LLM reasoning for retrieval instead of similarity search; 98.7% accuracy on FinanceBench (vs vector RAG baselines); SDK with local mode (pip install pageindex) and cloud mode; ~$0.001/page indexing cost; ideal for financial/legal/medical/technical documents; MIT

results.name: amazon-s3-vectors
results.title: Amazon S3 Vectors
results.summary: AWS cloud object storage with native vector support — 'vector buckets' hold vector indexes (up to 10,000 per bucket, up to 2 billion vectors per index at GA) queryable via dedicated APIs with no infrastructure to provision, up to 90% lower cost than purpose-built vector databases per AWS; metadata key-value filtering per vector; SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS encryption with per-index customer-managed keys; natively integrated with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Amazon OpenSearch Service; announced in preview July 2025, reached general availability December 2, 2025 with a 40x per-index scale increase over preview.

results.name: claude-mem
results.title: Claude Mem
results.summary: kb wiki + Claude Code built-in memory cover our needs; adds SQLite + Chroma + worker complexity without clear benefit

results.name: immich
results.title: Immich
results.summary: Production-ready self-hosted Google Photos alternative with AI search; not agent tooling but solid self-hosted media infrastructure.

results.name: asi-evolve
results.title: ASI-Evolve
results.summary: Impressive autonomous research-loop results but arbitrary code execution per round, no stated license, and very new (2026 academic repo)

results.name: event2vector
results.title: Event2Vector (event2vec)
results.summary: Python/PyTorch library for interpretable, composable embeddings of discrete event sequences — learns one vector per event type and represents a sequence as the composition (vector sum under the linear additive hypothesis) of its events, so trajectories support word2vec-style arithmetic; geometries include Euclidean, hyperbolic (Möbius addition), spherical, stereographic, rotation, Heisenberg, affine, and product; scikit-learn-style fit/transform/most_similar API; `pip install event2vector`; MIT; paper in PMLR vol. 282 (arXiv:2509.12188)

results.name: gbrain
results.title: gbrain
results.summary: kb wiki already provides persistent typed records with relationships and search

results.name: meridian
results.title: Meridian
results.summary: GPU-accelerated document processing pipeline — Docling (8 load-balanced instances) for PDF layout detection, Qwen3-VL via vLLM for table/figure/formula reading, Ollama for embeddings, Qdrant for vector storage; stateless Celery workers on CPU calling long-lived GPU services over HTTP; measured at 118 pages/min on a single H200; includes text-only path (pypdfium2, 1000 docs/min on CPU); Apache-2.0

results.name: synapse-memory-layer
results.title: Synapse (memory-layer)
results.summary: Early-stage, self-hosted persistent memory backend for LLMs (Claude Desktop, Claude Code/VS Code via MCP) that stores structured 'memory atoms' plus immutable evidence 'signals' in Postgres+pgvector behind a write-quality/critic/risk-gate commit pipeline; roadmap includes routing low-confidence questions to specific human experts and folding their answers back into memory.

results.name: maxun
results.title: Maxun
results.summary: Capable no-code web data platform with MCP support and LLM extraction, but early-stage and AGPLv3 copyleft limits commercial embedding

results.name: llama-index
results.title: LlamaIndex
results.summary: Open-source Python data framework for building LLM/RAG and document-agent apps: data connectors, indices/graphs, retrievers, and query engines to augment LLMs with private data, with 300+ integration packages (LLMs, embeddings, vector stores) on LlamaHub. Pairs with the commercial LlamaParse/Parse agentic-OCR platform. MIT.

results.name: paperless-ngx
results.title: Paperless-ngx
results.summary: Mature self-hosted document management system — useful for archiving research docs but not an agent tool or developer library

results.name: embeddinggemma-2
results.title: EmbeddingGemma 2
results.summary: Google DeepMind's 740M-parameter open multimodal embedding model — maps text, code, images, video, and audio into one 768-dim vector space; modular encoders (270M text-only to 740M full); 8K context window; runs on-device (191MB RAM for text-only on Pixel 11 Pro); Matryoshka truncation to 512/256/128 dims; built on Gemma 4; Apache 2.0

results.name: scann
results.title: ScaNN
results.summary: Google Research library for efficient large-scale vector similarity search — anisotropic vector quantization (AVQ) for Maximum Inner Product Search plus SOAR indexing, partition/score/rescore search pipeline, native Python and optional TensorFlow APIs, AVX/NEON-optimized x86/ARM wheels; powers Vertex AI Vector Search; Apache-2.0

results.name: faiss
results.title: FAISS
results.summary: Meta's C++/Python library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors — billion-scale datasets, GPU acceleration (CUDA/ROCm), multiple index types (HNSW, NSG, IVF, PQ), L2/dot-product/cosine similarity; 40K+ stars, MIT

results.name: nashsu-llm-wiki
results.title: LLM Wiki (nashsu)
results.summary: Cross-platform Tauri desktop app implementing Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern — ingests documents (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/EPUB/images/web clips) and incrementally compiles them into a persistent, interlinked wiki instead of re-deriving answers via RAG each query; ships a knowledge-graph visualizer (sigma.js/graphology, 4-signal relevance, Louvain community detection), optional LanceDB vector search, a tool-using chat agent, a local token-protected HTTP API plus MCP server for Claude Code/Codex, and an Obsidian-compatible vault output; ~21k GitHub stars; GPLv3

results.name: okf-agent-memory
results.title: OKF Agent Memory
results.summary: Git-native persistent memory framework for AI coding agents — a compact push-layer behavioral codex (AGENTS.md, ~100-150 tokens) enforced through Agent Action Grammar (AAG), plus a pull-layer knowledge bundle (OKF v0.2 Markdown+YAML) searched via a pure-Go embedded MCP server with sub-300us in-memory BM25; ships a linter enforcing AAG's token budget, ASCII-only syntax, and tool-signature parity rules

results.name: iai-personal-memory-engine
results.title: iai — Personal Memory Engine
results.summary: Fully local MCP-based personal memory engine for AI assistants — ambient capture, three-tier memory (episodic/semantic/procedural), custom storage engine (Hippo), clustering (MOSAIC), HD substrate (LilliHD), Rust embedder; macOS-only, English-only, MIT

results.name: clm
results.title: CLM (Contrastive Language Model)
results.summary: Open-weights, self-hostable classification model positioned as a drop-in alternative to TypeSafe AI's Jev — a frozen Qwen3-8B encoder plus two 20M-param trainable projection heads (state/action) trained with bidirectional InfoNCE contrastive loss; serves the same three typed-question primitives (Choice, Noul, Score) behind a TypeSafe-compatible API; reference head is ~75MB (Apache-2.0); reports up to 9x lower zero-shot latency and, with lightweight fine-tuning, SOTA verifier accuracy on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (87.6%) and DeepSWE (81.6%) at 4-6x Jev's speed

results.name: hnswlib
results.title: HNSWlib
results.summary: Header-only C++ library (with Python bindings) implementing HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graph search — the standalone reference implementation of the HNSW algorithm by Yury Malkov and Dmitry Yashunin; incremental index construction, element deletion/update, custom C++ distances, L2/inner-product/cosine spaces; Apache-2.0

results.name: openai-python-sdk
results.title: OpenAI Python SDK
results.summary: Official Python client for the OpenAI API — GPT, o-series, Codex, DALL-E, Whisper, embeddings; typed Pydantic models, async support, streaming, function calling; MIT, PyPI

results.name: huggingface-inference-providers
results.title: Hugging Face Inference Providers
results.summary: Unified API gateway routing inference to 15+ backend providers (Groq, Together AI, Cerebras, Replicate, etc.) via a single HF token; OpenAI-compatible, multi-task (LLM, VLM, image gen, embeddings, speech), with provider selection policies (:fastest, :cheapest, :preferred)

results.name: qwen25-coder-32b
results.title: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct
results.summary: Alibaba's 32.5B-parameter code-specialized open-weight LLM — 64-layer transformer with GQA (40Q/8KV), 128K context via YaRN, trained on 5.5T tokens including source code and synthetic data; coding abilities reported as matching GPT-4o; Apache-2.0

results.name: ovis-vl-embedding
results.title: Ovis-VL-Embedding
results.summary: Omni-modal embedding model (2B and 9B variants) built on Qwen3.5 backbone — encodes text, images, visual documents, and video frames in a shared representation space; 77.46 overall on MMEB-v2 (78 datasets), 80.47 on visual document retrieval; no modality-specific projection heads, last-token hidden state as embedding; for multimodal RAG, cross-modal search, document retrieval

results.name: crawl4ai
results.title: Crawl4AI
results.summary: Best-in-class async web-to-Markdown crawler for agent/RAG pipelines, but Docker API has had dense critical CVEs; library mode is safe to pilot

results.name: memoose
results.title: Memoose
results.summary: Local, no-API-key dual-path memory system for coding agents — SQLite knowledge graph, CLI + 26 MCP tools + skills/hooks harness; procedures stored as self-evolving 'procedural graphs' (steps as nodes, edges carrying conditions/advice/pitfalls) after Google's Procedural Graphs paper (arXiv 2609.09153)

results.name: ruview-wifi-sensing
results.title: RuView WiFi Sensing Platform
results.summary: Interesting hardware+agent integration with a Claude Code plugin and MCP server, but beta software requiring physical ESP32 hardware for core capabilities

results.name: repowise
results.title: repowise
results.summary: Local-first codebase-intelligence engine: index a repo once and keep it current per-commit, then serve it to coding agents via ~11 task-shaped MCP tools plus a CLI, local dashboard, VS Code extension, and a zero-LLM PR bot. Builds a five-layer index (dependency graph across 19 languages, git behavioral signals, generated wiki, mined architectural decisions, deterministic 1–10 code-health scores with concrete refactoring plans), plus change-risk scoring, dead-code detection, and reversible command-output 'distill'. Structural index needs no API key and runs offline; AGPL-3.0 with a commercial license option.

results.name: agent-dispatcher
results.title: Agent Dispatcher — repository retrieval and specialist-role routing for Claude Code and Codex
results.summary: Claude Code plugin and Codex skill pack that routes a task to one of 27 specialist roles (engineering, design, testing, research, writing, operations) and assembles a bounded context packet of source excerpts using symbols, source text, code relationships, Git history, and stack-trace frames — rather than a full-repo dump. Ships 79 bundled local skills, references 31 external skills, 8 workflow recipes, a registry of 19 MCP servers, and 50 detection signals for role/skill selection. Standard retrieval runs locally with no model or network calls; optional features (model-assisted reranking, an external 'Jev' decision-engine API, an Onboarding Explorer, procedural learning from recorded outcomes) are off by default and require the operator's own provider configuration. Installs via `claude plugin marketplace add` + `claude plugin install` for Claude Code, or `python3 install_codex.py` for Codex (installs one skill to `~/.agents/skills/agent-dispatcher/`). Invoked with `/agent-dispatcher:agent-dispatcher <request>` (Claude) or `$agent-dispatcher <request>` (Codex); roles can be forced directly (e.g. `$agent-dispatcher reviewer`). Verification is explicit: each role defines what evidence counts as done and reports which checks ran, passed, or were left unverified. Requires Python 3.10+, Git, and an authenticated Claude Code or Codex; native Windows is unsupported (WSL recommended). MIT license, single maintainer, repo created 2026-09-19 with ~50 GitHub stars and 4 forks as of this review.

results.name: lm-studio
results.title: LM Studio
results.summary: Desktop application for downloading, managing, and running local LLMs with GUI chat, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API server (localhost:1234), MLX and llama.cpp engines, built-in model search with VRAM fit estimation, GPU offload controls, voice transcription, and Bionic agentic assistant; JS/Python SDKs, MCP client support, headless daemon (llmster), LM Link encrypted remote inference; free for personal and commercial use; macOS/Windows/Linux

results.name: localai
results.title: LocalAI
results.summary: Open-source local AI engine — drop-in OpenAI/Anthropic/ElevenLabs API compatibility across 60+ backends (llama.cpp, vLLM, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion, MLX, etc.); supports LLMs, vision, voice, image, video on any hardware (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel/Apple/Vulkan/CPU); multi-user auth with quotas, built-in agents with MCP/RAG/tool use, distributed cluster mode, fine-tuning UI, WebRTC realtime audio; MIT

results.name: langflow
results.title: Langflow
results.summary: Heavy visual-builder platform with native MCP-server export; too large for direct adoption but worth monitoring for MCP workflow integration patterns.

results.name: redis-iris
results.title: Redis Iris
results.summary: Redis's context-and-memory platform for AI agents (announced May 18, 2026) — bundles real-time structured/unstructured data retrieval (Context Retriever), short- and long-term agent memory (Agent Memory: interaction history, user preferences, persistent attributes), and continuous data sync from source-of-record systems (Redis Data Integration) into one product, layered on existing Redis Search and LangCache semantic caching

results.name: tolvi
results.title: Tolvi — Engineering Decision Vault
results.summary: Solid CAG/RAG dual-mode decision-capture design but pre-1.0, small project, and overlaps with kb already in use

results.name: unstructured
results.title: Unstructured
results.summary: Open-source document ETL library — partitions 60+ file types (PDFs, Word, HTML, images, emails) into structured elements (Title, NarrativeText, Table, etc.) with layout ML enrichment, OCR, chunking, and embedding; connectors for 40+ sources/destinations; MCP server (Unstructured Transform) for agent-driven document processing; Apache-2.0, 15k+ stars

results.name: n8n
results.title: n8n
results.summary: Fair-code workflow automation platform (TypeScript) — visual node-based editor plus custom JS/Python code, 400+ integrations, native AI/agent capabilities (LangChain-based AI nodes, MCP client and server support), triggers/webhooks/schedules; self-hostable via Docker or paid n8n Cloud; Sustainable Use License + n8n Enterprise License (fair-code, not OSI open source); ~204k stars

results.name: polars
results.title: Polars
results.summary: Rust-core columnar DataFrame library with a multi-threaded, vectorized (SIMD) query engine and lazy query optimizer; Python/Rust/Node/R APIs, Apache Arrow memory model, streaming out-of-core execution, and readers/writers for CSV/JSON/Parquet/Delta/Arrow/databases/cloud storage. MIT.

results.name: mempalace
results.title: MemPalace
results.summary: Local-first AI memory with 96.6% R@5 retrieval, 33 MCP tools, verbatim storage, and pluggable backends; strong benchmarks and Claude Code integration make it worth trialing

results.name: sparse-memory-lm
results.title: sparse-memory-lm (product-key memory on a 21M model)
results.summary: Hobby research repo testing product-key memory layers (Lample et al. 2019; Meta 'Memory Layers at Scale') on a small model — a 21M-parameter Llama-style decoder plus a learned table of up to 16.8M rows × 384 dims (6.4B values, ~384 rows / 33M values read per token) matches a ~114M dense model's perplexity on 500M Wikipedia tokens; 4-bit table memory-mapped from NVMe generates ~114–140 tok/s using 0.4GB VRAM (prompt prefill slow from page faults); portable Triton kernels verified on RX 9070, MI350X, H100/H200; bolting a table onto pretrained Qwen3.5-0.8B did not help; Apache-2.0

results.name: duckdb
results.title: DuckDB
results.summary: High-performance in-process analytical (OLAP) SQL database. Rich SQL dialect (window functions, correlated subqueries, nested types), zero-config, embeddable; runs as a standalone CLI and as clients for Python, R, Java, Wasm, etc., with direct querying of CSV/Parquet files and pandas/dplyr integration. MIT.

results.name: dspy
results.title: DSPy
results.summary: Stanford NLP framework for programming (not prompting) LLMs via typed signatures, composable modules, and automatic prompt optimization; 35k stars, 433+ contributors, production use at scale — relevant for building optimized LLM pipelines

results.name: torchtune
results.title: torchtune
results.summary: PyTorch-native post-training library by Meta — composable building blocks (not trainers) for SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, GRPO, quantization, evaluation; YAML-driven recipes under 600 LOC; composable parallelism (FSDP2, TP, SP, CP, expert parallel for MoE); in-backward optimizer fusion; works on single 24GB GPU to multi-node clusters; v0.6 stable; Apache 2.0

results.name: rag-anything
results.title: RAG-Anything
results.summary: All-in-one multimodal RAG framework from HKU's Data Intelligence Lab, built on LightRAG — parses PDFs/Office/images/audio/video via MinerU, Docling, or PaddleOCR, then builds a multimodal knowledge graph linking text, tables, equations, and images; three query modes (text, VLM-enhanced, direct multimodal); 23,500+ GitHub stars; MIT

results.name: sdf
results.title: sdf
results.summary: Michael Fogleman's Python library for building 3D (and 2D) models from signed distance functions — primitives (sphere, box, torus, cylinder, cone, Platonic solids) composed with boolean ops (union, difference, intersection, including smooth/blended variants), transforms (translate, rotate, scale, twist, bend), and repetition (linear/circular arrays); meshes via Marching Cubes and exports STL natively plus 20+ formats (OBJ, PLY, ...) via meshio; also renders 2D SDFs from text/images for extrusion; actively maintained (pushed 2026-09-30); MIT.

results.name: outlines
results.title: Outlines
results.summary: Structured generation library by .txt — guarantees LLM outputs conform to JSON Schema, Pydantic models, regex, grammars, or Python types via constrained decoding (FSM-based token masking); works with transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, OpenAI, Gemini; Jinja prompt templates, function calling inference, batch generation; Rust core (outlines-core) for performance; 65M+ downloads; trusted by NVIDIA, Cohere, HuggingFace, vLLM; Apache-2.0

results.name: paddleocr
results.title: PaddleOCR
results.summary: PaddleOCR provides three product lines for document understanding — PP-OCRv6 scene text recognition, PP-StructureV3 document-structure-to-Markdown/JSON conversion, and the PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B-parameter vision-language model for full document parsing across 109 languages

results.name: jina-ocr-v1
results.title: Jina-OCR-v1
results.summary: End-to-end document-to-Markdown OCR model (3.4B total / 570M active MoE) with FastMTP speculative decoding (K=3, ~2x decode speed on L4) — scores 91.14 OmniDocBench, 83.4 olmOCR-Bench, 2.57 pages/s on A100; handles text, tables, math, handwriting, 100+ languages; runs via Transformers or vLLM; hosted via Jina Reader API; CC BY-NC 4.0 (weights)
